The residue of $-69$ modulo $6$ is the integer $0\le r<6$ such that

$$
-69≡r\,(\text{mod}\,6).
$$

**Method 1**

To find the residue $r,$ we need to write $-69$ as an integer multiple of $6,$ plus the residue $r.$

We note that $-69≡3\,(\text{mod}\,6)$ because

$$
-69=(-12)\cdot 6+3.
$$

Therefore, the residue of $-69$ modulo $6$ is $3.$

**Method 2**

We can use the addition property:

$$
\begin{aligned}-69 & ≡-69+0 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) \\  & ≡-69+12\cdot 6 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) \\  & ≡-69+72 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) \\  & ≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,6)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the residue of $-69$ modulo $6$ is $3.$
